newsitem.title: USA: Argentine politics not affecting economy - official.
newsitem.headline: Argentine politics not affecting economy - official.

text.p: Allegations of corruption that have dominated Argentine politics in recent weeks have not affected the country's economy, an Argentine financial official said Friday.
Joaqun Cottani, financial representative of Argentina, said that the country's economy was benefitting from a positive international climate and the upward momentum of the domestic business cycle.
"The economy has bottomed out and is recovering," Cottani said, forecasting 3.0 percent growth in 1996 and citing 5.0 percent in 1997 as a "conservative estimate."

Last month, former Argentine Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo levelled corruption charges at several senior officials. The officials, along with President Carlos Menem, adamantly rejected the allegations.
"The fate of the economy has been detached from political noises, which are in fact nothing but a very healthy discussion of challenges ahead in Argentina," Cottani said.

Cottani predicted that Argentina would have little problem rolling over its debt coming due in 1997. Total Argentine debt costs, including principal and interest payments, will rise to 15.3 billion pesos in 1997 from 11.7 billion this year.
"We don't see any problem rolling over debt next year," Cottani said. "We priced our (previous) bond correctly and there was a good reception ... We try to be realistic in our pricing."
In October, Argentina issued a $1.0 billion global bond 445 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
